nextAction.summary: Translation loop: 292 chunks, in order. Per chunk - read source/clean/pNNNN.txt for its page range, translate against the glossary, flag anything uncertain rather than smoothing it, write translation/<id>.md, then mark it done.
nextAction.notes: Every blocking terminology decision is settled (glossary/decisions.md); 0 terms are 'open'. The glossary is DESIGNED to grow here: append proper nouns and cited-text titles as they appear, and fix each one on first occurrence. glossary/terms-candidates.json holds 559 ranked candidates not yet judged. Flag, do not guess: node tools/32-chunk.mjs done <id> "unsure: ...".

decisions: Target language: Vietnamese. Deliverable: Markdown, translation-only (no bilingual layout).
Repair happens at CID level via our own content-stream interpreter, NOT by regex over decoded text.
source/raw/glyphs/ is the permanent audit trail and is never edited. Everything downstream is a reproducible transform.
Every repair-table entry requires TWO independent signals that agree. Score alone is not sufficient - see FINDINGS.md 8.5.
CIDs with no decisive evidence are left UNREPAIRED rather than guessed; each keeps a value that decodes to a valid Tibetan syllable.
Reference (do not copy) the existing Vietnamese Bo De Dao Thu De Quang Luan and the Snow Lion English translation for terminology checking only.

The outline is built from the book's OWN contents (dkar chag, pp. 8-20) cross-checked against the printed sa-bcad headings - two independent sources that must agree. 284/284 agree exactly. Do not rebuild it from heading detection alone.
Nesting depth comes from the RANK of the contents' indent column, not from rounding onto a fitted grid: the columns drift ~0.9pt, so a grid fit would be a judgement call dressed up as arithmetic.
Three places where the printed indentation skips a level are the SOURCE's own structure and are kept as printed, not normalised (recorded in source/outline.json notes).
Chunks start on section boundaries. Leaf sections longer than 5 pages are split into labelled parts (part: '2/8', startsAtHeading: false) so an artificial break is never mistaken for a section break.

SCOPE: translate everything. All 978 pages are chunked except the 13 contents pages (pdf 8-20), which are regenerated from the translated section titles at assembly rather than translated as prose - otherwise the index would drift from the headings it indexes.
pdf 21-23 is ROOT TEXT (Namo Guru Manjughosaya + the homage verses), not front matter. It carries no sa-bcad heading, so any chunking that starts at the first heading silently drops it. Chunk c004.
openQuestions: Phase 4: whether to enable experimental Agent Teams for the translation-quality skill, or run single-session (current assumption: single-session).

chunks.section: [front matter: title pages and publisher data]

flags: unsure: སྟག་རྩེའི་སྒྲུབ་མཆོད rendered 'đại lễ tu cúng Taktsé' - Taktsé read as a place name; could be a rite name

chunks.section: [root text: opening homage and pledge to compose, before the first sa-bcad heading]
flags: unsure: source spells Vikramasila as བྲི་ཀཱ་མ་ལ་ཤཱི་ལ (bri-), not the usual བི་ཀྲ་མ་ཤཱི་ལ - translated as Vikramasila, oddity noted
unsure: རྒྱ་ནག་སྟོང་ཁུན་རྒྱལ་པོ - Tongkhun taken as a Chinese ruler's name, transliterated; unsure: བྱིན་ལེན rendered 'phép thọ nhận thức ăn' from Vinaya context

unsure: p0053 line 1, སྤྲོ་སིང་བ་བྱས་ནས — this string occurs exactly once in the entire 978-page corpus and is not a normal spelling. I read it as སྤྲོ་བ + the intensifier སིང་ (cf. སྤྲོ་བ་སིང་ངེ་), hence 'làm cho tâm phấn khởi hân hoan'. Per the no-normalising rule I did not silently correct it to སྤྲོ་སེང / སྤྲོ་བ་བསྐྱེད, but the reading is inferred from one occurrence.

unsure: p0053, benefits 2–4 of the twenty (བློ་གྲོས / བློ / བརྟན་པ) — Tibetan uses three near-synonyms for intellect/steadiness in a row, then ཤེས་རབ as the fourth. I rendered them tuệ / trí / sự kiên định / trí tuệ to keep four distinct words, but no Vietnamese convention fixes which is which; the assignment of 'tuệ' to བློ་གྲོས and 'trí' to བློ is my choice, not a settled equivalence.

unsure: p0053, benefit 11, སངས་རྒྱས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་དགོངས་པར་འགྱུར་བ — དགོངས་པ here is the plain verb 'hold in mind', not the glossary's noun sense མật ý (abhiprāya). Rendered 'đoái nghĩ đến'; 'hộ niệm' was rejected as adding protection the Tibetan does not state (that is benefit 12).

unsure: p0054, the note on བསླབ་བཏུས — the whole remark is about three Tibetan words that differ by a vowel/letter (བརྟན་པ vs མོས་པ vs བརྟུན་པ). Vietnamese can carry the three senses (kiên định / tin ưa / siêng năng) but not the fact that the variance is orthographic, so a reader cannot see why the note exists.

unsure: p0054, བཀུར་བའི་ཞིང rendered 'ruộng tôn kính'. The idiom is 'field/object of veneration'; I kept the field metaphor because it is in the Tibetan, but Vietnamese 'ruộng' will pull the reader toward 'phước điền' (field of merit), which is a different compound. A ruling would help.

unsure: p0055, ཐེ ཡན་ལག triad དཔེ་དང་གཏན་ཚིགས་དང་ལུང rendered 'thí dụ, chánh lý và giáo chứng'. གཏན་ཚིགས is the pramāṇa term hetu, usually 'nhân' in Vietnamese logic texts, but 'nhân' collides with nhân/quả and with ལས; 'chánh lý' is my compromise and is not an established equivalence.

unsure: p0055, Lotus verse line 8, བྱེ་བ་ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་དཔེས — bye ba (10^7) and khrag khrig (a far larger scale unit) form an idiomatic 'countless myriads'. I wrote 'ức triệu thí dụ' as a compound quantity; any numerically precise Vietnamese rendering would assert magnitudes the idiom does not fix.

unsure: p0055 ends mid-verse-line (དེ་ལ་ནམ་ཡང་འདོད་པ་ཅུང་ཟད་); the negating verb མེད falls on p0056, in c017. Vietnamese requires the negation before the noun, so 'không bao giờ có chút mong cầu…' pulls that མེད back across the chunk boundary. c017 must not translate མེད again.

unsure: p0053 line 1 opening, བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔས་དེའི་བསམ་པ… — the Tibetan does not repeat who the bodhisattva is or whose བསམ་པ is meant; c015 established the pair (Sutasa's son / prince Candra). I left both unnamed ('vị bồ-tát' / 'người ấy') rather than resolving the reference.

unsure: བརྫེས་པ / གཟར་བ at p0057 line 1 - two bare items in the Vinaya list, not qualified by the preceding མགོ་བོ་གཡོགས་པ; left untranslated and marked in the text rather than glossed as modes of head-covering
unsure: དོ་ཀེར in མགོ་དོ་ཀེར་ཅན at p0057 line 1 - no word for hair in the clause; rendered "đầu [do ker]" with the term left unresolved

unsure: སྣོད at p0056 (སྣོད་བརྟག་པ, སྣོད་དུ་ཤེས་ན, and twice in the Kinh Tam-muội Vương verse) rendered 'pháp khí', NOT the glossary's provisional 'bình chứa'. The glossary note scopes 'bình chứa' to the three-faults-of-the-vessel simile (heading 5.1.3.1); here the sense is a fit recipient of teaching, and 'khảo sát bình chứa' would read in Vietnamese as examining an actual jar. Needs a ruling on whether the two senses share one rendering.

unsure: བརྫེས་པ and གཟར་བ at p0057 line 2 (in མགོ་བོ་གཡོགས་པ་དང་བརྫེས་པ་དང་གཟར་བ་དང་གཉའ་གོང་དུ་བསྣོལ་བ་དང་ལྟག་པར་བསྣོལ་བ) - two items in the Vinaya list of head/robe arrangements to which one does not teach. Neither is settled: rendered '[trùm đầu] xốc lên' and '[trùm đầu] để lệch' from the bare root senses (raised; steep/slanting), with the object supplied in brackets. The parallel members (head covered; crossed at the nape; crossed at the back of the head) are secure.

unsure: the first syllable-stack of p0057 line 2 is ambiguous in the render at scale 4 - the decoder gives བརྫེས་པ, but བརྗེས་པ ('exchanged, reversed') is visually near-identical at this zoom and would change the reading. Not a decoding regression, just an unresolved reading; recorded so it can be checked at higher zoom.

unsure: མགོ་དོ་ཀེར་ཅན at p0057 line 3, first item of the hat/crown/garland/turban list. Verified against the page image (the syllable is དོ, not ཐོ/བོ), and it occurs exactly once in the whole 978-page corpus. དོ་ཀེར is unattested to me; rendered 'người [để tóc] dựng đứng trên đầu' on the strength of ཀེར = erect plus the company it keeps (headgear). The bracketed 'tóc' is supplied and could be wrong - the item may be a turban or topknot term.

unsure: རབ་རྒྱས in the Kinh Tam-muội Vương verse at p0056 (རབ་རྒྱས་བདག་གིས་མ་བསླབས་ཞེས) read adverbially, 'Ta chưa từng học rộng'. It could instead be a vocative/name addressed to the requester, which would change the line to a form of address. No second signal either way.

unsure: བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ in the same verse taken as referring to the requester, so '[như ngươi]' is bracketed in as supplied. If it refers to a third party the bracket is wrong; the Tibetan does not say.

unsure: ཡོ་བྱད at p0056 rendered 'tư cụ'. The identical phrase བདག་གི་བདེ་བའི་ཡོ་བྱད occurs in the prose on p0055, inside c016's range, which is not yet translated - whichever wording c016 fixes should govern and this chunk be aligned to it.

note (not a doubt): this chunk carries TWO outline headings, not one - s023 (5.2.4, ཡུལ་གང་ལ་བཤད་པ་དང་མི་བཤད་པའི་ཁྱད་པར།) opens on p0056 and s024 (5.3, མཇུག་ཏུ་ཐུན་མོང་དུ་བྱ་བའི་ཚུལ།) on p0057. Both are stated in the body, at '###' and '##' per outline level + 1. The task brief said not to restate the section heading because the chunk is labelled part 2/2, but 5.3 begins inside this range and had not been stated by c016, so omitting it would have lost a heading.
unsure: p0058 line 1 མ་མཐའ་རེ་དང་ལྡན་པར་བྱ་སྟེ - the referent of རེ is not stated in the source; rendered "một [điều]" with the supplied head bracketed rather than resolved

unsure: the cited work སྙིང་པོ་ངེས་པར་བསྡུ་བ (p0058 line 13) is not identified. I rendered the title literally from its Tibetan components as *Tinh Yếu Quyết Định Tập* rather than guess at a Sanskrit original or an existing Vietnamese/Chinese title. If the work is one that already has a settled Vietnamese title, this rendering should be replaced.

unsure: ལྷ་བདུད་དུ་བབ་པ་ལྟར (p0058) — I translated the idiom literally, 'như vị trời sa xuống thành ma'. The sense is idiomatic (what should be divine/beneficial turns demonic/harmful), and a Vietnamese reader may not get it from the literal words; I did not gloss it, per the no-expansion rule.

unsure: མ་མཐའ་རེ་དང་ལྡན་པར་བྱ (p0058) is elliptical — 'should be endowed with at least one'. What the 'one' counts (one occasion? one of the listed points? one minimal measure?) is not stated in the Tibetan. I rendered 'chí ít cũng phải có được một phần' and supplied nothing further.

unsure: སྐྱོང་ཚུལ་མདོར་བསྡུས་ཏེ་བསྟན་པ (p0058, sub-topic 6.1.2) — the object of སྐྱོང་བ is unstated. 'cách thức gìn giữ' leaves it open as the Tibetan does; whether it is the reliance on the teacher, the meditation, or the practice generally cannot be settled from this chunk alone. The chunk covering 6.1.2 should confirm.

unsure: མཚན་ཉིད in the six-fold outline (p0059, items 1 and 2) — I took it as 'characteristic' and used the glossary's provisional 'tướng' rather than 'định nghĩa'. It reads stiffly in Vietnamese ('tướng của bậc thiện tri thức'), and these are heading strings that will recur for the whole of section 6, so a ruling would be worth making now; 'đặc điểm' would read better but is outside the glossary.

unsure: རིགས་ལ་གནས་པའི་གང་ཟག (p0058–p0059 verse) — I read རིགས as gotra ('chủng tánh'). The bare word can equally mean family/lineage in the ordinary sense, and the glossary's only ruling on རིགས (རིགས་སྐྱེས་པའི་མི) deliberately takes the flat reading 'dòng dõi'. Context (a verse on relying on a spiritual friend) favours gotra, but the verse itself supplies nothing decisive.

unsure: བཟོད་པ in the Bodhisattvapiṭaka list (p0059), positioned between ས (bhūmi) and ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན. I used the fixed 'nhẫn' (kṣānti). In lists of this shape the term is often the specific dharma-kṣāntis rather than the pāramitā, but the Tibetan says only བཟོད་པ, so nothing was added.

unsure: གྲོགས་སུ་འགྲོ་བ (p0058) rendered 'trở thành bạn hữu của phiền não', using the glossary's flat 'bạn hữu' for གྲོགས. The idiomatic sense is 'becomes an aid/ally to', which 'bạn hữu' carries only weakly in Vietnamese; I did not upgrade it to 'trợ duyên' because that word is not in the Tibetan.

note (not an error): the source at p0059 writes སྟེན་བྱེད་སློབ་མའི་མཚན་ཉིད with སྟེན་ rather than བསྟེན་. This is the correct present-stem agent form opposed to བསྟེན་བྱ in the preceding item, not a typo, and is translated as the agent ('người học trò nương tựa').

unsure: མཚན་ཉིད in the section heading (p0060 l.1) - characteristic or definition. Rendered "Tướng"; the section then enumerates ten defining marks, so "định nghĩa" is arguable. Flag required by decisions.md for the provisional ruling.

unsure: མཚན་ཉིད in the section heading. I used 'Tướng của bậc thiện tri thức đáng nương tựa' because c018 already renders this exact outline item that way in its six-fold list (line 68). But c021 renders the sibling heading སྟེན་བྱེད་སློབ་མའི་མཚན་ཉིད as 'Đặc điểm của người học trò nương tựa', while c018's list item 2 for the same heading says 'Tướng của người học trò nương tựa'. The four sibling headings under 6.1.1 are now inconsistent across chunks and need one ruling (decisions.md already asks for a flag rather than a silent choice here).

unsure: བསྟན་པའི་ཐ་མ་ལ་གང་ཕན in the Geshé Tönpa quotation (p0061). I translated literally, 'điều gì lợi ích cho chặng cuối của giáo pháp'. Two readings are open: (a) 'the last/final part of what has been taught' — i.e. among everything taught, what is of benefit at the end; (b) 'the final period of the teaching' (བསྟན་པ་ཐ་མ as the degenerate age), i.e. what benefits beings in that period. Nothing in the surrounding text decides it, so I kept a wording that does not commit to either.

unsure: མཐའ་བཞིའི་ཞལ་ནས (p0062). Read as a personal name and transcribed 'Tazhi'. མཐའ་བཞི occurs four other times in the corpus and every one of them is the doctrinal 'four extremes', never a name; this is the only occurrence with ཞལ་ནས. The name is not one I can confirm, and I could not check the glyphs against the rendered page (the PDF is not in the repo). If the reading is wrong, the whole clause changes.

unsure: ལི་མོའི་བུ (p0062), rendered 'Này con của Limo'. Parsed as a vocative naming Chengawa by his mother's or clan name. I could not verify that ལི་མོ is a name here rather than something else, and the phrase is inside a quotation, so I did not gloss it.

unsure: འགྲོ་བ rendered 'chúng sinh' (p0062, twice) collides with the fixed glossary entry སེམས་ཅན = chúng sinh. Phase 5 cannot tell the two apart in this chunk. Either a distinct rendering for འགྲོ་བ (e.g. 'loài hữu tình') should be fixed, or the collision should be recorded as deliberate.

unsure: དེ་ཉིད / དེ་ཁོ་ན་ཉིད (tattva) rendered 'chân như'. 'Chân như' is conventionally the Vietnamese for tathatā (དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད), which does not occur here; 'chân thật tánh' or 'thắng nghĩa' would keep the Sanskrit distinction. I chose the reading most legible to a Vietnamese Buddhist reader, but this is a term the book will use constantly and it should be fixed centrally before it spreads.

unsure: ཞི་གནས at p0061 rendered with the headword 'tịnh chỉ'. The fixed-set rule says use the headword where the term is being defined or argued about; here it appears inside the gloss of ཉེ་བར་ཞི་བ, which is a definition of a different term, so the case is borderline between 'tịnh chỉ' and 'thiền chỉ'.

unsure: verse line order in the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra quotation. The imperative ལ་བརྟེན sits at the end of the Tibetan's fourth line and governs བཤེས་གཉེན at the start of the first. I kept one Vietnamese line per shad and left 'hãy nương tựa' at the end of line 4, which reads as an afterthought in Vietnamese; the alternative would be to move the verb up and break the one-line-per-shad rule.
unsure: མི་དག in the Mitra-varga verse (p0061), read as མི 'person' + the plural particle དག and rendered 'người ta'. No other parse was checked against a second witness.
unsure: p0064 line 3 verse reads བསྒྲིན་ཅིང་གཟོ་ལ - rendered 'chuyên chú, khéo léo' only on the conjectural readings བསྒྲིམས and བཟོ; source not normalised, noted inline
unsure: p0063 line 1 གླ་བོ་དྲིན་དུ་གཅགས་པ་རེ་བྱེད་པ - obscure; rendered 'cảm kích tiền công như một ân nghĩa', its parallel to ཡོན་བཤད་རེ་བྱེད་པ not settled

unsure: p0063 གླ་བོ་དྲིན་དུ་གཅགས་པ་རེ་བྱེད་པའང་མེད་དེ — rendered 'chẳng từng làm lấy một lần việc đền đáp ân nghĩa của tiền công'. གླ་བོ is not securely identified (གླ = wage/fee; གླ་བོ could also be a musk deer, or a person). The reading taken is by parallel with the Nyentön clause, where ཡོན་བཤད is a talk given in return for offerings — so གླ (fee) is read as the counterpart of ཡོན (offering). This is an oral-Kadam colloquialism and the reading is not decisive.

unsure: p0063 ངེད་ཀྱི་སློབ་དཔོན་ཞང་བཙུན་ཀུན་ལ་མང་དུ་ཐོས་པའང་མེད — parsed as name ཞང་བཙུན + ཀུན་ལ་མང་དུ་ཐོས་པ ('extensive learning in everything'), giving 'đối với mọi mặt đều không có sự nghe học rộng nhiều'. unsure: བྱང་སེམས་དབང་ཐོབ་པ (p0617), rendered 'bồ-tát đã đắc tự tại'. Read as vaśitā (mastery over the absorptions), not as the glossary's དབང་ = 'quán đảnh' (initiation, from c005), which would make a substantively different claim about who the exceptions are. No entry exists for this sense.

unsure: ཉེ་བར་གཏོད་པ (p0618, ×2), rendered 'đặt [tâm] sát vào'. Reading and Vietnamese both provisional. It needs to be settled against whatever c182 fixed for the bare གཏོད་པ of this section's own heading (སེམས་དམིགས་པ་ལ་གཏོད་པ), which was still pending when this chunk was translated — the two must not collapse into one Vietnamese phrase.

unsure: སེམས་...་དེ་ལ་གཡེང་བར་མི་བྱེད་པའི་ཐབས (p0618). The ལ is ambiguous between 'not letting the mind wander FROM the basic object' and 'not letting it wander WITH REGARD TO it'. Rendered with the neutral 'không tán loạn nơi cái sở duyên căn bản' so the Vietnamese does not resolve what the Tibetan leaves open.

unsure: རྩེ་གཅིག rendered 'nhất tâm' throughout (3×), following the glossary headword རྩེ་གཅིག་པ = 'sự nhất tâm' and c176 in this same division. The competing corpus form 'chuyên nhất' (c014/c033, and the registered སེམས་རྩེ་གཅིག་པ = 'tâm chuyên nhất') is still live and unruled; that entry's own note already requests the ruling.

unsure: p0620 — ལུང་སྔ་མ་ལས་ཤེས་བཞིན་ལྕགས་ཀྱུ་དང་འདྲ་བར་གསུངས. The 'former citation' is the Madhyamakahṛdaya verse just quoted, but that verse reads ཤེས་རབ་ལྕགས་ཀྱུ ('hook of WISDOM'), not ཤེས་བཞིན. I translated both exactly as written — 'móc sắt trí tuệ' in the verse, 'tỉnh giác ... giống như móc sắt' in the prose — and did NOT harmonise them. Either Tsongkhapa is reading the verse's ཤེས་རབ as vigilance, or ལུང་སྔ་མ points back to his own preceding prose (ཤེས་བཞིན་གྱི་ལྕགས་ཀྱུས་གཙགས). Verifier should check this is not read as a translation error.

unsure: bare དྲན་པ rendered 'chánh niệm' (×13) rather than the glossary's bare-form entry 'niệm'. The glossary's own note on that entry says the ruling is open and only the compound དྲན་པ་དང་ཤེས་བཞིན = 'chánh niệm và tỉnh giác' is settled; 'chánh niệm' is attested in 12 chunks of the corpus, and 'sợi dây niệm' / 'niệm có sức mạnh' would not read as Vietnamese Buddhist register. Not a re-decision made lightly — needs the owner's ruling.

unsure: ཞུམ་པ at p0622–p0623 rendered 'sự thối lui' instead of the glossary's 'thối chí' — see the newTerms note. The sense here is the mind's withdrawal/sinking (equated by Buddhaśānti with བྱིང་བ), not loss of motivation.

unsure: p0621 ཤེས་པ་འཕངས་ལེགས་པར་བསྟོད་དེ, rendered 'nâng cao khéo léo cái thế của tâm thức'. Read as the idiom འཕང་བསྟོད་པ = raising the pitch/level of awareness, matched against རིག་པའི་གཟེངས་ཀྱང་སྨད ('hạ thấp cái thế vươn cao') two clauses later, which is its explicit opposite. The reading is from that internal contrast, not from a lexicon entry.

unsure: p0623 བཅོམ་པས in the Deśanāstava commentary — the Tibetan does not say what does the overcoming. I rendered 'do bị [điều ấy] chế ngự' with the agent bracketed and unnamed rather than resolving it to excitement-and-distraction.

note: p0623 source oddity — U+0F0C (non-breaking tsheg) appears where an ordinary tsheg belongs, in གསུངས་པས༌གློད་པ་རབ༌བྱས་པས (offsets 491, 501). Typographic only, no effect on the reading; left untranslated-over, not normalised.
